import html from string import Template # Template for rendering an event invitation. The placeholders will be filled with escaped content. INVITATION_FORMAT: str = """

${event_title}

${event_description}

Date: ${event_date}

Additional Notes

${additional_notes}

""" def render_event_invitation( event_title: str, event_description: str, event_date: str, additional_notes: str ) -> str: """ Render a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- event_title : str Title of the event. event_description : str Full description of the event. May contain line breaks. event_date : str Date string for the event. additional_notes : str Any user‑provided notes about the event. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string ready for rendering in a web page. Notes ----- All user supplied content is escaped using `html.escape` to protect against XSS and other injection attacks. The template is defined using :class:`string.Template` to keep the formatting readable and avoid accidental placeholder injection. """ # Escape all user-provided values safe_title = html.escape(event_title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(event_description, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(event_date, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(additional_notes, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") template = Template(INVITATION_FORMAT) return template.substitute( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes )
